comparison.objective: Candidate sets and mechanically locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2207 operates a handheld dryer and manipulates articulated hair to dry exposed and occluded regions while the mannequin head remains fixed.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests rigid driver/wrench counterholding and functional cycling; PR-2207 tests switch operation, dryer pickup and aiming, deformable lock separation, airflow exposure, and thermal control.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, nut retention, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, and released clearance; PR-2207 requires at least 90% water removal on every hair patch, temperature at most 50°C, fixed-head integrity, power off, parking, and a one-second released hold.
comparison.reason: Deformable hair exposure and geometry-dependent drying are meaningfully different from threaded stop adjustment and jam-nut locking; PR-2207 lacks a formal task.json, demonstrated full-task allowance, full demo, model run, and media, without making the novelty distinction ambiguous.
